Subject: Options for switching to annual prepay

Hi Marissa,

We’re looking at moving Acme’s Redwood billing from the current monthly plan to an annual prepay to simplify forecasting. High-level asks:
- What term discounts do you offer for 1-year vs 2-year prepay?
- Can we structure a ramp schedule so we don’t have to lock full commit in month 1?
- Any concessions you’d consider around unused capacity credits or true-ups?

We’re targeting a decision by next week if the economics look right. Can you send a quote we can share with procurement?

Thanks,
Alice Wu

Acme Corporation

Hi Alice 9

Thanks for the clear ask. I’ve attached a concise quote and a draft SOW that reflects two annual prepay options plus a 2-year committed option:

Summary (see attached PDF for line-item math):
- 1-year annual prepay: 10% term discount off list; monthly ramp allowance (first 3 months at 40% of yearly commit with true-up at month 4).
- 2-year annual prepay: 18% term discount; 9-month linear ramp to full commit.
- Add-on: Reserved GPU burst pool available for Q4 spikes at a discounted rate (applies to both terms).

We can offer a limited unused-capacity credit for the first year only (up to 8% of committed spend) if you prepay and sign within 10 business days. That concession requires approval from my manager.

Attached: redwood_annual_quote_v2.pdf, SOW_draft.docx

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm which term you prefer (1Y vs 2Y) and target commit level.
2) I’ll route the credit concession to finance and legal; if approved I’ll update the quote and send for signature (DocuSign).

Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week to walk the tables.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 08:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Options for switching to annual prepay

Hi Alice,

Answers inline:
1) Overages: the 40% figure is a billing floor for the ramp months (we invoice for 40% of the annual commit in months 1-3 regardless of usage). If you exceed that in any billing month, overage usage is billed at the discounted committed unit rate (not list rates). We also offer a one-time true-up at the end of month 3 to reconcile to actuals so you aren’t charged at list prices mid-quarter.

2) Unused-capacity credit: pathway is manager + finance approval. It is only applied as an accounting credit against future Redwood invoices (non-refundable cash). It does not carry forward past the second year unless explicitly negotiated in a 2-year contract. If you go over in year 2, the credit will be consumed first; excess usage above the credit will be billed at the committed rate.

3) Reporting: yes, monthly usage reports, token-level cost breakdowns, and per-route latency/SLAs are included in the Redwood Console for committed accounts. We can add a clause in the SOW that confirms report cadence and retention window.

I’ve asked Rafael to confirm whether the ramp/true-up mechanics will require any additional engineering-side gating.

Best,
Marissa
